plumbing.summary: Everything passed: gofmt, go vet, the tests of every package the change touches, and every acceptance test.
plumbing.review:
1. **[P1] Codex’s MCP allowance never reaches the real server.** [codex.go:337](repo/internal/synth/codex.go#L337) sets `INVARIANT_TOOL_ALLOWANCE` on Codex’s environment, but [codex.go:243](repo/internal/synth/codex.go#L243) omits MCP `env`/`env_vars`. Installed Codex 0.163.0 clears its MCP child’s environment and forwards a whitelist excluding this variable. Each replacement server therefore gets a fresh allowance. The [acceptance fixture:185](repo/cmd/invariant/provider_limits_accept_test.go#L185) masks this by inheriting the entire environment. Explicitly forward the variable and test the real filtering behavior.

2. **[P2] A dropped Claude stream can renew the dollar budget.** [claudecode.go:139](repo/internal/synth/claudecode.go#L139) subtracts prior reported cost, but [claudecode.go:322](repo/internal/synth/claudecode.go#L322) records cost only from a closing result. Paid work followed by a connection loss without that result contributes zero cost, restoring the full budget on retry and understating cumulative usage. Account for incomplete attempts conservatively; add coverage with paid work before the disconnect. The current [disconnect fixture:237](repo/internal/synth/provider_retry_accept_test.go#L237) contains no preceding work.

3. **[P2] Ordinary MCP failures are retried as provider outages.** [provider.go:29](repo/internal/synth/provider.go#L29) treats generic connection phrases as provider errors. [codex.go:367](repo/internal/synth/codex.go#L367) recognizes MCP startup failures but still passes their diagnostics through that classifier. A handshake failure containing `connection closed: initialize response` consequently receives provider backoff and misleading failure reporting. Exclude MCP startup failures and cover the complete diagnostic; the [ordinary-failure fixture:341](repo/internal/synth/provider_retry_accept_test.go#L341) tests only the bare message.

The changes stay within the allowed files and match surrounding Go style. Documentation covers the requested behavior and decision references. I found no added agent network/host access or secret disclosure. Ratified tests are unchanged; the factory reports passing checks, which I did not rerun during this read-only review.

VERDICT: changes needed — fix MCP allowance forwarding, incomplete-attempt cost accounting, and MCP error classification, with regression coverage.

usage.summary:
Implemented #261’s retries, shared limits, cumulative usage, saved failures that publish no PR, and documentation updates. All checks passed on test run 3: gofmt, go vet, affected packages, and every acceptance test.

Implementation choice: shared MCP allowances use a protected per-run counter file. The merger must record the provider-retry decision, including its refinement of D-0154’s timeout rule.
